figs.title: Shear centre locations for open sections
figs.caption: The shear centre S is the point a transverse load must pass through to bend the section without twisting it. It lies outside the web of a channel, at the corner of an angle, at the centroid of a Z by antisymmetry, and at 4R/π from the centre of a thin semicircle, beyond the arc.

figs.title: Equivalent spring of an inclined strut
figs.caption: A displacement δ along the load stretches a strut inclined at θ to that direction by δ cos θ, and the strut force projects back with a second cos θ. The equivalent spring is (EA/L) cos²θ, so a strut at 60° supplies a quarter of its axial stiffness.

figs.title: Dead load versus follower load
figs.caption: A dead load keeps its direction and is conservative, so a frequency falls to zero at divergence and the energy method finds it. A follower load turns with the tip; in the Ziegler column two frequencies merge at Pl/k = 2.09 into flutter, which only the kinetic method reveals.

figs.title: Ritz convergence with the number of terms
figs.caption: With admissible trial functions on a cantilever under uniform load, the tip deflection is within 5% with one term and within 1% with two. The root moment comes from second derivatives and is still about 5% low with eight terms, approaching the exact value from below.

figs.title: Energy landscape below, at and above P_cr
figs.caption: For a rigid bar on a rotational spring the upright state sits in an energy well below P_cr. At P_cr the well flattens to a quartic, and above P_cr the upright state becomes a hilltop between two buckled minima at θ = (P/P_cr) sin θ.

figs.title: Beam-column interaction with amplification
figs.caption: First yield under axial load and end moment follows P/P_y + (M₀/M_y)/(1 − P/P_cr) = 1. The amplification bows the straight stocky-section line inward, and a slender member reaches its limit at P_cr with only a small moment.
